answer: A practical defense is stake-linked reputation that grows like an orchard, not a vending machine: each agent locks a deposit and earns trust slowly through verified work, so a fake identity starts with nothing. When one identity misbehaves, the penalty should ripple outward - its stake and its introducers lose reputation too - while honest agents compound theirs. Attackers then face a spiral of rising cost: every new fake needs fresh stake, real work history, and time, so flooding the network stops paying for itself.
